name: Bali
tagline: Temple smoke, emerald rice terraces and surf at the end of the day
description:
Bali packs startling variety into an island you can drive across in three hours. In the south, Seminyak and Canggu hum with beach clubs, surf schools and brunch cafés; inland, Ubud sits among ravines and rice terraces where gamelan practice drifts out of village pavilions every evening; to the north and east, volcanoes rise above crater lakes and quiet black-sand coves.

What makes the island unforgettable is its living Hindu culture. Families place woven palm-leaf offerings on doorsteps, dashboards and shop counters every morning, temple festivals halt traffic with processions in white and gold, and on Nyepi, the Day of Silence, the entire island switches off, airport included.

Traffic in the south is genuinely slow, so base yourself in two areas rather than day-tripping everywhere: perhaps Ubud for culture and the Bukit Peninsula or Sanur for the sea. The dry season runs roughly from May to September; the wet months bring short, heavy afternoon downpours, greener landscapes and lower prices.

airport.name: I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport

safety.notes: Violent crime is rare, but bag snatching from passing motorbikes, ATM skimming and scooter accidents are real risks. Only drink arak at reputable venues, and keep sunglasses and phones zipped away around the temple monkeys.

tipping: Upscale restaurants add tax and service of up to about 21% (the 'plus-plus' on menus), but tipping drivers, guides and spa therapists Rp20,000–50,000 is warmly appreciated.
gettingAround: There is no useful public transport for visitors, so use Grab or Gojek for short hops and hire a car with driver for about $45–60 a day. Only rent a scooter if you are experienced and hold an international license with a motorcycle endorsement.
tips: Pay the Rp150,000 tourist levy online through the official Love Bali platform before you fly to avoid queues at the airport.
Carry a sarong and sash in your daypack; most temples require them and the loaner stalls expect a donation.
See temples and rice terraces early in the morning, when the light is soft and the tour vans from the south haven't arrived yet.
Use ATMs inside banks or supermarkets and change money only at authorized changers with posted rates, counting your cash before you leave the counter.
Book a driver for full-day trips at a fixed rate covering up to ten hours and fuel, and agree upfront which parking and entrance fees are extra.
Drink bottled or filtered water and ice from factory-made cylinders with a hole in the middle; many cafés now offer free refills for reusable bottles.
etiquette: Never step on the small canang sari offerings on the ground; walk around them.
Cover shoulders and knees at temples and tie a sash at the waist; women who are menstruating are asked not to enter.
Use your right hand to give or receive money and objects, and never touch anyone's head, which is considered sacred.
Give way to temple processions and never climb shrines, walls or sacred trees for a photo; tourists have been deported for it.

neighborhoods.name: Ubud
neighborhoods.blurb: The island's cultural heart, ringed by rice fields and river gorges, with nightly dance performances, yoga studios and excellent vegetarian cafés.

neighborhoods.name: Seminyak
neighborhoods.blurb: A polished beach strip of boutique shopping, sunset beach clubs, spas and some of Bali's best restaurants.

neighborhoods.name: Canggu
neighborhoods.blurb: A laid-back surf town turned digital-nomad hub, with rice paddies squeezed between smoothie-bowl cafés, surf breaks and lively bars.

neighborhoods.name: Uluwatu
neighborhoods.blurb: Clifftop Bukit Peninsula country of white-sand coves, world-class reef breaks and the famous sea temple; stunning but spread out.

neighborhoods.name: Sanur
neighborhoods.blurb: A calm, reef-protected east-coast town with a long beachfront promenade, sunrise views and fast boats to Nusa Penida.

dishes.name: Babi guling
dishes.description: Whole spit-roasted suckling pig stuffed with turmeric, lemongrass and chili paste, served with shards of crackling, lawar and a fiery soup.

dishes.name: Bebek betutu
dishes.description: Duck rubbed in rich base genep spice paste, wrapped in banana leaves and slow-cooked for hours until it falls off the bone.

dishes.name: Sate lilit
dishes.description: Minced fish or chicken mixed with grated coconut and spices, pressed around lemongrass stalks and grilled over coconut husks.

dishes.name: Nasi campur
dishes.description: A mound of rice surrounded by small portions of whatever the warung cooked that day: shredded chicken, tempeh, sambal matah and fried peanuts.

dishes.name: Lawar
dishes.description: A spiced mix of finely chopped long beans, grated coconut and minced meat, served at almost every ceremony and village feast.

events.name: Nyepi (Balinese New Year)
events.description: On the eve, giant ogoh-ogoh demon effigies are paraded through villages, then the whole island observes 24 hours of silence with no lights, traffic or flights; the date follows the lunar calendar.

events.name: Bali Arts Festival
events.description: A month-long celebration of dance, gamelan and crafts at Denpasar's main arts center, launched with a huge street parade and running into July.

events.name: Bali Kite Festival
events.description: Village teams fly enormous traditional kites, some longer than ten meters, over the fields and beaches near Sanur to the sound of gamelan orchestras.

events.name: Ubud Writers & Readers Festival
events.description: Southeast Asia's leading literary festival brings authors, poets and musicians to Ubud for several days of talks, workshops and performances.

attractions.name: Tanah Lot
attractions.description: This 16th-century sea temple perches on a rock outcrop that becomes an island at high tide, with surf pounding its base. At low tide priests at the freshwater spring below bless visitors, but the real show is sunset, when the temple turns to silhouette against a molten sky.
attractions.bookingTip: Check the tide times so you can walk out to the base at low tide, and arrive an hour before sunset to claim a clifftop spot.

attractions.name: Uluwatu Temple
attractions.description: Clinging to a limestone cliff some 70 meters above the Indian Ocean, this temple offers one of Bali's most dramatic sunset panoramas. Stay for the Kecak fire dance in the clifftop amphitheater, where a chanting circle of bare-chested men accompanies an episode of the Ramayana.
attractions.bookingTip: Buy Kecak tickets (sold separately) online or by 17:00, and stow sunglasses, hats and phones, because the resident macaques are expert thieves.

attractions.name: Tegallalang Rice Terraces
attractions.description: Sculpted into a steep valley north of Ubud, these terraces are still watered by the centuries-old subak system of shared irrigation channels. Walk down to the valley floor and up the far side for the best angles, and expect farmers to ask for small donations at bridges and paths.
attractions.bookingTip: Arrive by 08:00, before the swing operators and tour groups, and carry small notes for the informal path donations.

attractions.name: Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary
attractions.description: More than a thousand long-tailed macaques roam this jungle sanctuary, where moss-covered temples and a ravine laced with giant banyan roots make it feel like a film set. The monkeys are cheeky rather than cuddly, so keep bags zipped and let them come to you.
attractions.bookingTip: Buy tickets online to skip the gate queue, and leave snacks, plastic bags and loose items at your hotel.

attractions.name: Tirta Empul
attractions.description: Balinese Hindus have bathed in this temple's spring-fed pools for more than a thousand years, moving along a row of carved spouts to purify body and mind. Visitors may join the ritual in a rented sarong; watch how locals pray first and follow their order along the fountains.
attractions.bookingTip: Come before 09:00 and bring a change of clothes; you will need to rent the required sarong to enter the purification pools.

attractions.name: Mount Batur
attractions.description: The sunrise trek up this active volcano is Bali's classic adventure: a two-hour climb in the dark, then breakfast cooked in volcanic steam as dawn lights up Mount Agung and the crater lake below. The trail is steep and gravelly but manageable for anyone of average fitness.
attractions.bookingTip: Book through a licensed operator that includes the mandatory local guide and hotel pickup, which is usually around 02:00.

attractions.name: Ubud Palace
attractions.description: Ubud's royal family still lives in parts of this palace, whose carved stone gates and gilded doors form the backdrop for nightly Legong and Barong dance performances. By day the outer courtyards are free to wander; by night it is one of the best-value culture shows on the island.
attractions.bookingTip: Buy dance tickets (about Rp100,000) from the sellers at the gate during the afternoon and arrive 20 minutes early for a front-row seat.

attractions.name: Seminyak Beach
attractions.description: A wide sweep of golden-gray sand where beanbags and umbrellas bloom every afternoon and beach clubs turn up the DJs for sunset. The surf is powerful and rips can be dangerous, so swim only between the red-and-yellow flags.
attractions.bookingTip: Reserve a daybed at the beach clubs a day ahead in high season, and expect a minimum spend.

attractions.name: Agung Rai Museum of Art
attractions.description: Set in lush gardens south of central Ubud, this museum traces Balinese painting from classical Kamasan narrative works to the European-influenced styles of the 1930s. It also hosts dance rehearsals and gamelan lessons, so music often drifts across the lotus ponds.
attractions.bookingTip: Check the weekly schedule for evening dance performances on the garden stage, which make a lovely pairing with a gallery visit.

attractions.name: Pura Ulun Danu Bratan
attractions.description: Tiered pagoda roofs appear to float on Lake Bratan in the cool central highlands, framed by misty mountains about 1,200 meters above sea level. Pair it with the Bedugul fruit market and the twin-lakes viewpoint for a refreshing day away from the coast.
attractions.bookingTip: Come early before the clouds roll in, and pack a light jacket, since it is around 10°C cooler than the coast.

hotels.name: Tebing Wangi Private Villas
hotels.description: Twenty-two villas cling to the Bukit cliffs, each with its own infinity pool staring straight out over the Indian Ocean. A cliff lift drops to a private cove, and the spa specializes in warming Balinese boreh spice scrubs.

hotels.name: Griya Teratai
hotels.description: A family compound turned 16-room boutique hotel, set around lotus ponds five minutes' walk from the palace. Rooms have carved teak doors and outdoor rain showers, and breakfast is served on your private terrace.

hotels.name: Pondok Ombak Hostel
hotels.description: A friendly hostel ten minutes' walk from the beach, with a small pool, air-conditioned dorms with privacy curtains and cheap surfboard hire. Family-style nasi campur dinners every night make meeting people easy.

hotels.name: Sawah Lestari Jungle Resort
hotels.description: Bamboo-and-thatch villas step down a jungle ravine beside working rice paddies, linked by stone paths and an inclined lift. Mornings start with yoga in an open pavilion above the river, and the restaurant grows much of its produce on site.

hotels.name: Jero Kediri Heritage House
hotels.description: Stay in a restored noble family compound among rice fields ten minutes from Tanah Lot, with carved pavilions and a private family temple. The hosts invite guests to help make the day's offerings each morning.

hotels.name: Karya Studio Hotel
hotels.description: Architect-designed rooms of rammed earth, recycled teak and polished terrazzo, hung with works by young Ubud painters. The rooftop pool looks across Pengosekan's rice fields toward Mount Agung on clear mornings.

restaurants.name: Warung Klungkung Guling
restaurants.description: A family warung that roasts one whole pig over coconut husks every morning and sells out by early afternoon. A heaped plate of crackling, spiced pork, lawar and a fiery broth costs about $3.

restaurants.name: Rimba Api
restaurants.description: An open-kitchen tasting menu built entirely on Indonesian ingredients, from Bali-grown cacao to smoked Jimbaran mackerel, served on a terrace above a jungle ravine. Ten courses reinterpret village dishes like lawar and betutu with serious finesse, and a full vegetarian menu runs alongside.

restaurants.name: Kopi Sawah Terrace
restaurants.description: An airy café perched above the terraces, serving single-origin Kintamani pour-overs, smoothie bowls and banana pancakes drizzled with palm-sugar syrup. Come early for misty views before the crowds arrive.

restaurants.name: Pantai Karang Seafood Grill
restaurants.description: Pick your snapper, prawns or clams from the ice trays, choose a marinade of chili sambal or sweet soy, and eat at a clifftop terrace after the Kecak show. The grilled fish comes with rice, water spinach and three homemade sambals.
restaurants.signatureDish: Ikan bakar (grilled snapper) with sambal matah

restaurants.name: Salt & Frangipani
restaurants.description: A breezy Mediterranean bistro a block back from the beach, doing wood-fired flatbreads, grilled octopus and mezze with Balinese twists such as sambal matah labneh. The wine list is strong for Bali, where imported bottles are heavily taxed.

restaurants.name: Rumah Bebek Tampaksiring
restaurants.description: A garden restaurant among rice fields on the road to the holy springs, where duck is rubbed with base genep, wrapped in banana leaf and slow-smoked for hours. Order a whole bird a day ahead if you are a group.

restaurants.name: Daun Muda Plant Kitchen
restaurants.description: An all-vegan kitchen cooking Indonesian classics with tempeh fermented in-house, including a rich jackfruit rendang and gado-gado with cashew sauce. Cold-pressed jamu tonics of turmeric and tamarind are the house specialty.

restaurants.name: Warung Danau Mujair
restaurants.description: After the sunrise trek, refuel at this lakeside warung with mujair nyat-nyat, crispy Lake Batur tilapia in a turmeric-and-chili sauce. Wash it down with coffee from Kintamani's arabica farms while the volcano looms overhead.

experiences.name: Batur Sunrise Volcano Trek
experiences.description: Pickup at 02:00, a flashlight-lit climb with a licensed Kintamani guide, and a summit breakfast of eggs and bananas steamed in volcanic vents as dawn breaks over Mount Agung. Descend past steaming craters and finish with a soak in a lakeside hot spring.

experiences.name: Balinese Market-to-Table Cooking Class
experiences.description: Start early in Ubud's morning market choosing spices with your teacher, then cook eight dishes, from base genep paste to sate lilit and black-rice pudding, in a family compound kitchen. Everyone eats together at a long shared table.

experiences.name: Holy Spring Blessing & Village Healer Visit
experiences.description: A Balinese guide explains the offerings and prayers before you join the water blessing at Tirta Empul, then visits a village balian, a traditional healer, for a consultation and herbal jamu. Respectful, unhurried and far more meaningful than a rushed photo stop.

experiences.name: Uluwatu Clifftop Kecak & Seafood Evening
experiences.description: Head down to the Bukit Peninsula in the late afternoon, stroll the temple clifftops at golden hour with a guide, take reserved seats for the Kecak fire dance, then dig into grilled seafood on the sand at Jimbaran Bay.
